Summary

Command: kubectl logs frontend-76d98597b9-g5zrg -n shop --tail=100 (success, return code 0)

Key Finding: The frontend pod (nginx-based) is consistently failing to reach its backend upstream service.

Pattern observed (20:35:45 – 20:38:53 UTC):
Health checks (GET /healthz from kube-probe) are succeeding normally every 5 seconds — pod itself is healthy.
All requests to /api/items (from client 10.244.1.43, user-agent "Wget") are failing with 504 Gateway Timeout.
Nginx error logs repeatedly show: upstream timed out (110: Operation timed out) while connecting to upstream targeting http://10.96.10.144:8000/items.
Failures occur roughly every 4–8 seconds, consistently, with no successful /api/items responses in the entire log window.

Diagnosis implication: The frontend/nginx itself is fine (passes health checks), but it cannot establish a connection to the backend service at 10.96.10.144:8000 (likely the "items" API/backend service in the shop namespace). This points to a backend service issue — e.g., the backend pod(s) are down, unresponsive, overloaded, or there's a network/connectivity problem between frontend and backend (service 10.96.10.144:8000), rather than a frontend-side problem.

Suggested next step: Investigate the backend service/pods behind ClusterIP 10.96.10.144:8000 (check pod status, logs, and connectivity) to find why connections are timing out at the TCP/connect level (not just slow response).

Command: kubectl logs frontend-76d98597b9-kt2jr -n shop --tail=100 (success, return code 0)

Summary: Logs from the nginx-based frontend pod in the shop namespace, covering startup through ~4 minutes of runtime (20:35:25–20:39:03).

Key findings:
Startup: nginx 1.27.5 started normally at 20:35:25, spawning 10 worker processes using the epoll event method.
One-time error: At 20:35:28, a single upstream connection failure occurred — connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while proxying GET /api/items to upstream http://10.96.10.144:8080/items, resulting in a 502 response to the client (10.244.1.43, Wget agent). This appears to be a transient issue (likely the backend service wasn't ready yet).
Recovery: Starting at 20:35:34, all subsequent /api/items requests succeeded with 200 status (response size 38 bytes), continuing consistently through the end of the log (20:39:03).
Health checks: Regular kube-probe/1.37 health checks (GET /healthz) from 10.244.2.1 return 200 every ~5 seconds throughout, with no failures — indicating the pod itself is healthy and ready.
Traffic pattern: Client 10.244.1.43 (Wget) repeatedly polls /api/items at irregular intervals (every few seconds), all succeeding after the initial failure.

Conclusion: The frontend pod is currently healthy and functioning correctly. There was a single transient 502 error early on due to the backend (upstream at 10.96.10.144:8080) not being immediately available, but connectivity was restored within ~6 seconds and has remained stable since.
